examples.solution_text:
The inner function is $f(x)=3x^{2}+5x+2$, with $f'(x)=6x+5$. No adjustment is needed.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int (6x+5)e^{3x^{2}+5x+2}\,dx\\&=e^{3x^{2}+5x+2}+C\end{aligned}$

The inner function is $f(x)=2x^{2}+6x+5$, with $f'(x)=4x+6$. Since $8x+12=2(4x+6)$, retain a factor of $2$ outside the integral.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int (8x+12)e^{2x^{2}+6x+5}\,dx\\&=2\int (4x+6)e^{2x^{2}+6x+5}\,dx\\&=2e^{2x^{2}+6x+5}+C\end{aligned}$

The inner function is $f(x)=6-2x^{2}$, with $f'(x)=-4x$. The adjustment is negative because $3x=-\frac{3}{4}(-4x)$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 3xe^{6-2x^{2}}\,dx\\&=-\frac{3}{4}\int (-4x)e^{6-2x^{2}}\,dx\\&=-\frac{3}{4}e^{6-2x^{2}}+C\end{aligned}$

The inner function is $f(x)=x^{3}+2$, with $f'(x)=3x^{2}$. Adjust by $\frac{2}{3}$, then substitute the original limits.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{-1}^{0}2x^{2}e^{x^{3}+2}\,dx\\&=\frac{2}{3}\int_{-1}^{0}3x^{2}e^{x^{3}+2}\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{2}{3}e^{x^{3}+2}\right]_{-1}^{0}\\&=\frac{2}{3}e^{2}-\frac{2}{3}e^{1}\\&=\frac{2}{3}(e^{2}-e)\end{aligned}$

Write the inner function as $f(x)=5x^{-1}$. Its derivative is $f'(x)=-5x^{-2}$, so the adjustment is $-\frac{2}{5}$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 2x^{-2}e^{\frac{5}{x}}\,dx\\&=-\frac{2}{5}\int (-5x^{-2})e^{\frac{5}{x}}\,dx\\&=-\frac{2}{5}e^{\frac{5}{x}}+C\end{aligned}$

The inner function is $f(x)=2x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, with $f'(x)=x^{-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$. Retain the constant multiplier $3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int \frac{3e^{2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\\&=3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}e^{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\\&=3e^{2\sqrt{x}}+C\end{aligned}$

$\frac{d}{dx}\left(e^{2x^{2}+8x+3}\right)=(4x+8)e^{2x^{2}+8x+3}$.
Since $x+2=\frac{1}{4}(4x+8)$, use the derivative to recognise the primitive.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int (x+2)e^{2x^{2}+8x+3}\,dx\\&=\frac{1}{4}\int (4x+8)e^{2x^{2}+8x+3}\,dx\\&=\frac{1}{4}e^{2x^{2}+8x+3}+C\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: For g(x)=3x²+5x+2, g'(x)=6x+5. Thus the primitive is e^{3x²+5x+2}+C; differentiating recovers the complete integrand.
For g(x)=2x²+6x+5, g'(x)=4x+6 and 8x+12=2g'(x). The primitive is 2e^{2x²+6x+5}+C, whose derivative is the stated integrand.
For g(x)=6−2x², g'(x)=−4x. Since 3x=(−3/4)g'(x), the primitive is −(3/4)e^{6−2x²}+C. Its derivative is 3xe^{6−2x²}.
The derivative of (2/3)e^{x³+2} is 2x²e^{x³+2}. At x=0 the primitive is (2/3)e²; at x=−1 it is (2/3)e. Upper minus lower gives (2/3)(e²−e).
For g(x)=5/x, g'(x)=−5/x² on x≠0. Multiplying by −2/5 gives the required factor 2/x². Hence the primitive is −(2/5)e^{5/x}+C on each interval excluding zero.
For g(x)=2√x, g'(x)=1/√x on x>0. Therefore the derivative of 3e^{2√x} is 3e^{2√x}/√x, confirming the primitive 3e^{2√x}+C.
Differentiating e^{2x²+8x+3} gives (4x+8)e^{2x²+8x+3}. Since x+2=(4x+8)/4, the required primitive is (1/4)e^{2x²+8x+3}+C.
